meta.why: R2 had no definition of organ dysfunction in its citation pool; the gpt-5-mini run answered 'no organ dysfunction' for both true-sepsis cases by citing a statement about ordering lactate

normalisations.why: PDF text layer lost the space after the leading article
PDF text layer lost the space before the unit

propositions.statement: Sepsis is defined as life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection.
propositions.note: the operative clause for us is 'organ dysfunction' — R2's whole question

propositions.statement: Organ dysfunction can be identified as an acute change in total SOFA score >=2 points consequent to the infection.
remarks: The baseline SOFA score can be assumed to be zero in patients not known to have preexisting organ dysfunction.
propositions.note: THIS is the yardstick R2 was missing on 2026-08-07

propositions.statement: The baseline SOFA score should be assumed to be zero unless the patient is known to have preexisting (acute or chronic) organ dysfunction before the onset of infection.
propositions.note: matters for our S1b-type patients: chronic CHF/COPD does NOT get counted as the acute change

propositions.statement: A SOFA score >=2 reflects an overall mortality risk of approximately 10% in a general hospital population with suspected infection. Even patients presenting with modest dysfunction can deteriorate further, emphasizing the seriousness of this condition and the need for prompt and appropriate intervention, if not already being instituted.
propositions.note: the second sentence is the one that argues against reading a low score as reassurance

propositions.statement: Sequential [Sepsis-Related] Organ Failure Assessment Score. Respiration, PaO2/FIO2, mm Hg (kPa): 0 = >=400 (53.3); 1 = <400 (53.3); 2 = <300 (40); 3 = <200 (26.7) with respiratory support; 4 = <100 (13.3) with respiratory support. Coagulation, Platelets, x10^3/uL: 0 = >=150; 1 = <150; 2 = <100; 3 = <50; 4 = <20. Liver, Bilirubin, mg/dL (umol/L): 0 = <1.2 (20); 1 = 1.2-1.9 (20-32); 2 = 2.0-5.9 (33-101); 3 = 6.0-11.9 (102-204); 4 = >12.0 (204). Cardiovascular: 0 = MAP >=70 mm Hg; 1 = MAP <70 mm Hg; 2 = Dopamine <5 or dobutamine (any dose); 3 = Dopamine 5.1-15 or epinephrine <=0.1 or norepinephrine <=0.1; 4 = Dopamine >15 or epinephrine >0.1 or norepinephrine >0.1. Central nervous system, Glasgow Coma Scale score: 0 = 15; 1 = 13-14; 2 = 10-12; 3 = 6-9; 4 = <6. Renal, Creatinine, mg/dL (umol/L): 0 = <1.2 (110); 1 = 1.2-1.9 (110-170); 2 = 2.0-3.4 (171-299); 3 = 3.5-4.9 (300-440); 4 = >5.0 (440); Urine output, mL/d: 3 = <500; 4 = <200. Catecholamine doses are given as ug/kg/min for at least 1 hour. Glasgow Coma Scale scores range from 3-15; higher score indicates better neurological function.
propositions.note: six systems; R2 can now check the patient against each one instead of reasoning from whether a lactate was ordered

propositions.statement: Patients with suspected infection who are likely to have a prolonged ICU stay or to die in the hospital can be promptly identified at the bedside with qSOFA, ie, alteration in mental status, systolic blood pressure <=100 mm Hg, or respiratory rate >=22/min.
propositions.note: all three are available at triage — unlike SOFA, which needs labs

propositions.statement: Neither qSOFA nor SOFA is intended to be a stand-alone definition of sepsis. It is crucial, however, that failure to meet 2 or more qSOFA or SOFA criteria should not lead to a deferral of investigation or treatment of infection or to a delay in any other aspect of care deemed necessary by the practitioners.
propositions.note: the direct antidote to the failure mode we observed — a negative or unmeasurable score is explicitly NOT grounds for ruling sepsis out

propositions.statement: Septic shock is a subset of sepsis in which underlying circulatory and cellular/metabolic abnormalities are profound enough to substantially increase mortality.

Patients with septic shock can be identified with a clinical construct of sepsis with persisting hypotension requiring vasopressors to maintain MAP >=65 mm Hg and having a serum lactate level >2 mmol/L (18 mg/dL) despite adequate volume resuscitation. With these criteria, hospital mortality is in excess of 40%.
propositions.note: note 'despite adequate volume resuscitation' — at triage this is usually not yet establishable, which is itself the honest answer for R4

propositions.statement: Among non-ICU encounters in the validation cohort (n = 66 522 with suspected infection, of whom 1886 [3%] died), qSOFA had predictive validity (AUROC = 0.81; 95% CI, 0.80-0.82) that was greater than SOFA (AUROC = 0.79; 95% CI, 0.78-0.80; P < .001) and SIRS (AUROC = 0.76; 95% CI, 0.75-0.77; P < .001).
propositions.note: our setting is the ED — this is the number that applies, not the ICU one

propositions.statement: In the ICU, the predictive validity for hospital mortality of qSOFA above baseline risk (AUROC = 0.66; 95% CI, 0.64-0.68) was statistically greater than SIRS criteria (P = .01) but significantly less than SOFA (P < .001).
propositions.note: kept alongside the ED number so the contrast is citable rather than asserted
